questions.prompt: Why does a pending sync response belong to a generation rather than to a user, and where does the coordinator check it?

keyPoints.text: Matching the user id is not enough to detect a stale response.
keyPoints.quote: User identity alone is not a sufficient stale-response guard.

keyPoints.text: A log-out and log-in to the same account makes the id match again.
keyPoints.quote: The identifier matches again, but the old request belongs to a different session.

keyPoints.text: Every session change increments a counter that sync captures.
keyPoints.quote: The coordinator increments a generation on every setSession call

keyPoints.text: Queued work checks the generation before touching the outbox or network.
keyPoints.quote: Queued operations check the captured generation before reading the outbox or making a request.

keyPoints.text: In-flight work checks again before committing.
keyPoints.quote: In-flight operations check again before committing a result.

keyPoints.text: The refresh path checks on both sides of the credential request.
keyPoints.quote: The refresh branch checks before requesting new credentials and after refresh completes.

questions.prompt: Explain the acknowledgement boundary and the profile-update rule: what may be removed from the outbox, and how a delayed profile response avoids clobbering refreshed credentials.

keyPoints.text: Acknowledging is narrower than emptying the outbox.
keyPoints.quote: The acknowledgement boundary is narrower than clearing the outbox.

keyPoints.text: Only ids that were actually sent may be deleted.
keyPoints.quote: Only identifiers present in the sent batch may be removed

keyPoints.text: Today's adapter cannot produce foreign ids, so the filter is a safety net.
Events queued during the request survive into the next view.
keyPoints.quote: Events added while the request was pending remain in storage

keyPoints.text: A profile can be current while its captured token is stale.
keyPoints.quote: A returned user profile may be current while its captured access token is outdated

keyPoints.text: The returned user is combined with the current tokens.
keyPoints.quote: combines the returned user with the coordinator's *current* tokens

keyPoints.text: This keeps newer credentials instead of an old closure's.
keyPoints.quote: This preserves newer credentials instead of rebuilding authentication from an old closure.

questions.prompt: Be honest about the test coverage of the guard on sync.ts line 99: which half is exercised, which case is missing, and what the mutation runs showed.

keyPoints.text: Line 99 checks both the generation and the user id.
Existing tests switch only to a different user or to logged out.
keyPoints.quote: The existing tests only switch to a *different* user or to logged-out

keyPoints.text: So the identity half alone satisfies those tests.
keyPoints.quote: so the identity half alone is enough to pass them

keyPoints.text: The same-user re-login case has no test.
keyPoints.quote: is described above but has no test

keyPoints.text: Removing either half of the guard keeps the suite green.
keyPoints.quote: deleting either half of line 99 leaves all six coordinator tests green

keyPoints.text: The guard and its two halves are visible in runOnce.
